Select drive, check ahead, beside and behind for traffic, signal, and move from brake to accelerator only when the path is safe.
Accelerate gently with the ball of your foot on the pedal and your heel resting on the floor.
For a normal stop, check rear traffic in the mirrors, move from accelerator to brake and maintain steady brake pressure until stopped.

Before entering an intersection at a stop sign or red light, stop behind the stop line or crosswalk.

Stop at a flashing red signal and yield to traffic that is not required to stop.

why_how.text: Turn the steering wheel toward the desired direction of travel whether moving forward or backward.
Place both hands on opposite outer sides of the wheel at four and eight o'clock, using a firm but gentle grip for control and air-bag clearance.
Look behind the vehicle before getting in because the driver's seat may hide children or small objects.
Keep a foot on the brake when shifting the vehicle into reverse.
For backing, place the left hand at twelve o'clock on the wheel and the right arm along the passenger seat back while looking through the rear window.
Mirrors used during backing do not show the area directly behind the vehicle.
Use a rear-view camera when available, but do not depend on it alone because it may omit part of the area.
Back slowly with gentle acceleration, turning the wheel slightly toward the desired rearward path because steering is harder in reverse.
When backing through a turn, briefly check ahead and to the sides while continuing to look rearward until fully stopped.

why_how.text: A right turn at red is allowed unless a sign forbids it, after a complete stop and after all crossing vehicles and pedestrians clear the intersection.
A left turn at red is allowed only from the far-left lane of a one-way street into another one-way street, unless a posted sign prohibits that turn.
When a light changes to green, wait briefly before entering and do not assume that other road users will obey their signals or yield.
Even at green, wait before the intersection until traffic beyond it moves enough to let you clear it without blocking crossing traffic.
Before turning onto a road, verify a clear path and a gap large enough to cross, enter the proper lane and accelerate to traffic speed.
Do not turn or pull out in front of an approaching signaling vehicle without enough clear distance, because its driver may turn later or have left the signal on.
After stopping where cross traffic is hidden, edge forward to obtain a view before entering the intersection.

Drive on the roadway's right half unless one of the stated exceptions applies.
Passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction is a stated exception to the right-half roadway rule.
A road divided into at least three marked lanes is a stated exception to the right-half roadway rule.
A road designed and posted for one-way traffic is a stated exception to the right-half roadway rule.
Police directions or a traffic-control device may direct travel outside the normal right half of the roadway.
An obstruction may require driving left of center, but the driver must yield to oncoming traffic.
On a road with at least four lanes, the handbook directs travel in the right lane and use of the lane immediately right of center for passing and left turns.
